alex: FYI I'm seeing a big regression on /v1/stream after the 2312347000 runtime merge — p95 up ~3x for requests hitting dedicated-gpu-a :grimacing:
alex: Spike aligns with the rollout start around 10:05 PST
maria: Confirmed in logs: stream emits lots of tiny SSE frames and there's a ~10ms gap between chunks in many traces
sam: Any CI alerts?
perf-bot: staging-e2e CI perf check FAILED (streaming-latency): p95 +2.9x, p99 +4.1x. https://perf.redwood.example/runs/8942
olga: Grabbed a flamegraph from a canary instance. Hotspots are in serialize_frame() and kernel_selector::choose — interestingly the selector now prefers a deterministic single-thread kernel for short seq lengths
alex: We're also seeing increased KV cache hit rate but that shouldn't slow SSE. The selector flip to single-threaded cuBLAS for seq < 8 matches latency behavior
maria: Which PR touched that logic? tia, did your recent backoff/coalescer changes include kernel heuristics?
tia: Yes, my PR changed the coalescer window (2ms -> 3ms) and added a conservative kernel_pref: if (estimated_seq_len < 12) prefer_deterministic = true; to avoid nondeterminism in small-batch evals
sam: Could the coalescer be changing timing so flushes land in a distribution that triggers the deterministic kernel?
olga: I instrumented traces with coalescer on/off. Two effects: a ~6ms extra wait due to the 3ms coalesce window + scheduling, and flushes end up with many short prefixes so the kernel heuristic hits the deterministic branch more often
alex: Toggled coalescer off locally — latency returned to baseline in my tests
sam: So there are two interacting regressors: the kernel heuristic tweak is the primary regressor and the coalescer timing amplifies it for streaming traffic
olga: Bisect confirms kernel heuristic line in commit 7a1f3b2 is the main culprit. Coalescer change makes it worse under real SSE patterns but kernel_pref alone raises p95 ~45% in microbenchmarks
perf-bot: Bisect summary: culprit=commit 7a1f3b2 (kernel heuristic). Revert restores staging perf baseline
deploy-bot: Rollout paused for runtime/2026-03-18-merge; will not promote canaries
alex: Immediate action: partial revert of kernel_pref heuristic. Keep coalescer A/B so we can measure independently
sam: Also add a streaming microbenchmark to CI that simulates lots of short frames before unblocking kernel heuristic changes
olga: I'll open a revert PR and add a unit test asserting kernel_selector::choose prefers throughput kernel for streaming-pattern flushes unless determinism explicitly requested
tia: Sorry everyone — my intent was to make small-batch evals deterministic. I'll change to an explicit opt-in flag for deterministic kernels rather than a global heuristic
maria: Infra: pin older kernel policy on Dedicated pools until we validate revert. Watch KV cache hit patterns — coalescer affected eviction behavior slightly
sam: Assign follow-ups: olga -> bisect/revert + microbench, tia -> deterministic opt-in PR, infra -> pin. I'll file a tracking ticket
alex: Filed INF-1029: "Runtime: revert kernel-pref heuristic, add streaming microbench, opt-in deterministic flag" and assigned olga, tia, infra
olga: Quick numbers from local repro: baseline p95=68ms, after heuristic p95=184ms, revert -> 72ms
deploy-bot: Revert PR #3421-revert queued for staging merge; not yet in prod
maria: After revert we should still monitor KV hit rate — coalescer's timing tweak can nudge eviction patterns
tia: I'll update docs and mark deterministic as opt-in. Sorry for the breakage
sam: Post-revert we'll iterate on a safer heuristic: use a short histogram of recent seq lengths instead of static threshold, and require streaming-microbench pass before merges
olga: Revert merged to staging at 2312350200; canary looks stable so far. Watching for 15min then we can consider promotion
alex: Thanks — keeping rollout paused until we see post-revert CI and 15m canary stability. :thumbsup:
